title: Deaths of Abbey Brunish and Fazola, and his own illness
summary: The drummer died playing with Sharkey; Fazola died from overeating; Bourgeois was near death three years earlier.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: It's a shame he did one. He was playing the Sharky when he died. Supposed to fall on the Sharky's arms.
Yeah, yeah. He just played the bass. He was playing the Sharky when he died.
He was playing the Sharky's arms. He just passed out right after he ate or something like that.

He had a bad heart. Like Fazola knew he was going to die too. He quit the, what's the band now? The band had the amateur thing that Al Hurt played on. What was the band? Horace Hyde. Horace Hyde. He quit Horace Hyde to come back home, you see, so his mother could keep him on a strict diet. Well he'd eat the diet at home and come out and go to some restaurant and eat a big meal. You see, Fazola didn't die from drinking, he died from eating. He had a bad condition and he was, you know, supposed to be on a strict diet. He and I went in a restaurant in New York one day and ate and we came out walking on the street. He says, let's go in this Chinese place and get some Chinese food. I said, well, I'm full of killing him. Oh, come on. He had a big Chinese meal right on top of the other meal. He loved to eat. And I think that's what killed him, the food, you know.
That's what the hell is saying. Everybody says it.
He ate himself to death. And he was a young man, he shouldn't have died that young. For instance, look at me. Almost three years ago I was given up for death.
I bet you were pretty sick that morning.
Well, what about Coulomb? Did he die?
Yeah, Alec died recently. Well, he was kind of old, though. Alec was close to seventy.
